summaries.summary: Econometrics applies statistical and mathematical methods to the analysis of economic relationships, using data to estimate and test economic models. The learned society of the field, the Econometric Society, describes itself as "an international society for the advancement of economic theory in its relation to statistics and mathematics," and publishes the journals Econometrica, Quantitative Economics, and Theoretical Economics. In the American Economic Association's Journal of Economic Literature (JEL) classification, econometrics falls within category C, "Mathematical and Quantitative Methods," which includes the subcategory C5, "Econometric Modeling." Within the Library of Congress Classification the discipline is named in the schedule path "Mathematical economics. Quantitative methods--Econometrics" (class HB139). The Universal Decimal Classification places the closely related area of "Mathematical economics" at UDC 330.4.

summaries.summary: Labour economics (also labor economics) studies the workforce and the markets through which labour is supplied and hired. Encyclopaedia Britannica defines it as the "study of the labour force as an element in the process of production," explaining that "The labour force comprises all those who work for gain, whether as employees, employers, or as self-employed, and it includes the unemployed who are seeking work," and that the field "involves the study of the factors affecting the efficiency of these workers, their deployment between different industries and occupations, and the determination of their pay." In the American Economic Association's JEL classification the field falls within category J, "Labor and Demographic Economics." The Universal Decimal Classification groups it under UDC 331, "Labour. Employment. Work. Labour economics. Organization of labour."

summaries.summary: Economic history examines economic systems and economic life as they have developed over time. Encyclopaedia Britannica defines it as the "branch of historiography concerned with the history and development of economic systems and, more broadly, with the investigation of economic aspects of historical societies," noting that "The studies of history and economics were once closely related" and that political economists such as Adam Smith, Thomas Malthus, and Karl Marx "incorporated historical data into their analyses." The field is served by scholarly bodies including the Economic History Association, whose site (EH.net) hosts its annual meeting and publications. In the American Economic Association's JEL classification economic history forms its own top-level category, N, "Economic History."

summaries.summary: Public finance studies the revenue, expenditure, and debt operations of government and their effects on the economy. The Universal Decimal Classification gives the field a dedicated place at UDC 336.1, "Public sector finance. Government finance in general," nested within UDC 336, "Finance," alongside UDC 336.2, "Public revenue," and UDC 336.5, "Public expenditure. State expenditure." In the American Economic Association's Journal of Economic Literature classification the corresponding category is H, "Public Economics," which encompasses the subcategory H2, "Taxation, Subsidies, and Revenue." The field is served internationally by scholarly bodies such as the International Institute of Public Finance.

summaries.summary: International economics studies economic transactions and relationships among nations, centring on international trade and international finance. Encyclopaedia Britannica defines international trade, the field's core subject, as "economic transactions that are made between countries," among which "are consumer goods, such as television sets and clothing; capital goods, such as machinery; and raw materials and food," with such transactions "facilitated by international financial payments." In the American Economic Association's JEL classification the field forms top-level category F, "International Economics," whose subcategory F1 covers "Trade." The Universal Decimal Classification groups the area under UDC 339, "Trade. Commerce. International economic relations. World economy," with UDC 339.5 covering "Foreign trade. External trade. International trade" and UDC 339.7 covering "International finance."

summaries.summary: Financial economics studies the allocation of resources under uncertainty over time, including asset pricing, the behaviour of financial markets, and the financing decisions of firms and investors. In the American Economic Association's Journal of Economic Literature classification the field forms top-level category G, "Financial Economics," whose subcategory G1 covers "General Financial Markets" and which sits alongside the neighbouring economics categories in the same scheme. The Universal Decimal Classification places the area at UDC 336.7, "Money. Monetary system. Banking. Stock exchanges," within the broader UDC 336, "Finance," the same parent class under which public-sector finance and public revenue are also grouped. Scholarly societies in the field include the American Finance Association, publisher of The Journal of Finance.

summaries.summary: Economic geography works at the interface of economics and geography, studying the spatial distribution of economic activity. Encyclopaedia Britannica treats it within geography's human-geography branch, observing that "Economic geography has a long pedigree" and that "Its traditional focus has been the distribution of various productive activities--with subdivisions into, for example, the geography of agriculture, industrial geography, and the geography of services--and patterns of trade such as transport geography." The scholarly journal Economic Geography describes its remit as research that "deepens the understanding of geographical drivers and implications of economic processes on the economy and society." In the Universal Decimal Classification the cognate area of "Regional economics. Territorial economics" appears at UDC 332, within the economics class UDC 33.

summaries.summary: Demography is the scientific study of human populations. Encyclopaedia Britannica defines it as the "statistical study of human populations, especially with reference to size and density, distribution, and vital statistics (births, marriages, deaths, etc.)." The International Union for the Scientific Study of Population (IUSSP) likewise describes demography as "the scientific study of human populations primarily with respect to their size, their structure and their development," stating that its own mission "is to promote the scientific study of population, encourage exchange between researchers around the globe, and stimulate interest in population issues." In the Universal Decimal Classification the field has a dedicated top-level place at UDC 314, "Demography. Population studies."
